negative_findings.description: No MK bank was found publishing an explicit merchant acquiring price list (MSC/merchant discount rate per card scheme, POS terminal rental, e-commerce gateway fee) as a public, dated document. Public corporate tariffs cover accounts, transfers and business cards; acquiring pricing appears to be contract-negotiated.
negative_findings.result_summary: mk and en queries on 'провизија за трговец', 'прифаќање картички', 'POS терминал изнајмување', 'merchant acquiring price list' returned only general terms of business (STB) and third-party explainers, no numeric merchant pricing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Acquiring economics — the core of cash-vs-card merchant incentives — cannot be read directly from tariffs; it must be inferred from general terms, interchange regulation, media and merchant-side sources.

negative_findings.description: No published interchange-fee cap schedule or interchange-level disclosure specific to North Macedonia was located; the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems defines 'заменски надоместок' but no public per-scheme rate table was found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: mk query on интерчејнџ/меѓубанкарски надоместок returned law texts, a parliamentary amendment proposal (levica.mk) and media commentary on bank fee income, but no rate schedule.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without interchange rates, pass-through analysis from issuer tariffs to merchant costs stays qualitative.

negative_findings.description: Tariff documents for Силк Роуд Банка, Развојна банка на Северна Македонија, and Зират банка (Ziraat) were not surfaced by the queries run in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Combined mk query naming these institutions returned results only for CCB, Sparkasse, ProCredit, NLB and Capital.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of the smaller-bank tier is incomplete; Development Bank is not a retail issuer but Silk Road and Ziraat are.

negative_findings.description: No Macedonian-language public price lists were found for licensed non-bank payment institutions or e-money institutions; the local term set ('ценовник', 'тарифа на платежна институција') produced only the regulator's registers, not institution-level pricing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register pages found; individual institution tariffs not located because the entity list itself was not retrievable in this pass (nbrm.mk 403 on automated fetch).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Non-bank PSPs are the fastest-moving segment for cash-out/cash-in pricing and are missing from the tariff corpus.

negative_findings.description: Automated fetches of nbrm.mk and provizii.mk returned HTTP 403. Treated as bot defence, not as dead links.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of three planned WebFetch calls on these hosts returned 403 Forbidden with no body.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The two most valuable index/pointer sources for this cell need a browser-grade collector rather than a plain HTTP fetcher.

coverage_gaps.description: Tariff sources located for roughly 10 of the ~13 MK banks; Silk Road Bank, Ziraat Bank and Development Bank of NM remain uncovered, and savings houses (штедилници) were not scouted at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a per-institution mk query pattern '<bank name> тарифа надоместоци pdf' against the NBRM list of licensed banks and savings houses to close the roster.

coverage_gaps.description: Merchant-side documents (acquiring general terms, POS terms of use, e-commerce merchant agreements) were found only for Stopanska banka; equivalents from NLB, Komercijalna, Halkbank and UNIBanka were not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Target each acquirer's business/legal documents section with mk queries on 'општи услови за прифаќање платежни картички', 'договор со трговец', 'ПОС терминал услови'.

coverage_gaps.description: Most banks expose only the currently effective tariff; historical versions were observed only for Sparkasse and CCB. Without back-versions, fee time series must be built forward from now.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Start immediate periodic snapshotting of every tariff PDF, and mine web.archive.org for historical versions of the identified PDF URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: Key regulator and aggregator hosts (nbrm.mk, provizii.mk) block plain HTTP fetching, and most bank tariff PDFs use long URL-encoded Cyrillic filenames that change with each revision, so static URL lists will rot quickly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a browser-grade collector plus per-bank link-discovery crawlers that re-resolve the current tariff PDF from the bank's tariff landing page each run.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language versions of MK bank tariffs were not systematically checked; several banks publish EN tariff extracts which are easier to parse but may be abridged or stale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each bank, check the /en/ mirror of the tariff page and record whether the EN version is a faithful translation and equally dated.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions and independent ATM deployers / cash-in-transit or exchange-office cash access pricing are entirely absent from the current candidate set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retrieve the NBRM registers with a browser-grade fetch, enumerate licensed entities, and scout each entity's own 'ценовник/тарифа' page.

brief: North Macedonian bank tariff books are an unusually rich and legally mandated public corpus: every licensed bank publishes a dated 'тарифа/тарифник на надоместоци' for physical and legal persons, plus 'општи услови' and framework agreements, and the National Bank both prescribes a standardised fee vocabulary ('најрепрезентативни услуги', 'информативен документ за надоместоците') and runs a fee-comparison entry point. This pass located tariff sources for the large majority of MK banks (Komercijalna, Stopanska Skopje and Bitola, NLB, Halkbank, Sparkasse, ProCredit, UNIBanka, TTK, CCB, Capital) together with two aggregators (provizii.mk, bankometar.mk) and a trade-press change-detection feed. The hard boundary is merchant acquiring: no bank publishes numeric MSC, POS rental or e-commerce gateway pricing, so acquiring economics must be triangulated from Stopanska's public card-acceptance general terms, the interchange definitions in the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems, processor CaSys, and media/academic sources. Practical collection risk is technical rather than legal — nbrm.mk and provizii.mk bot-block plain fetchers, and tariff PDFs sit behind long URL-encoded Cyrillic filenames that change every revision, so link re-discovery plus immediate forward snapshotting is required.
